Row.Text: Adama Dramé is a Burkinabé percussionist.
Ali Ibrahim Touré (31 October 1939 - 6 March 2006) was a Malian singer and multi-instrumentalist.
Ami Koita (Djoliba, 1952), nicknamed "the diva of Mandinga music", is a Malian singer.
Ballaké Sissoko (born 1968) is a Malian player of the kora.
Boubacar Traoré (born 1942 in Kayes, Mali) is a Malian singer, songwriter, and guitarist.
Kandia Kouyaté is a Malian jelimuso (a female griot) and kora player.
Kassé Mady Diabaté was a Malian singer, musician and griot.
Mamadou Sidiki Diabaté (born September 23, 1982) is a prominent Mandé kora player and jeli from Bamako, Mali.
Mah Damba (born Mah Sissoko in Bamako, Mali, 1965) is a traditional griot singer.
Assitan Keïta, popularly known as Mamani Keïta (born 20 October 1965) is a singer and musician from Mali. Mamani means grandmother.

Mama Africa, was a South African singer, songwriter, actress, and civil rights activist. Her music was banned in South Africa, and her South African citizenship and right to return were revoked. Makeba thus became stateless, but she was soon issued passports by Algeria, Guinea, Belgium and Ghana. Throughout her lifetime she held nine passports and was granted honorary citizenship in ten countries.
Salif Keïta (born 25 August 1949) is a Malian singer-songwriter, referred to as the "Golden Voice of Africa".
Sona Jobarteh (born 1983) is a Gambian multi-instrumentalist, singer and composer.

Toumani Diabaté (10 August 1965 – 19 July 2024) was a Malian kora player. In addition to performing the traditional music of Mali, he was involved in cross-cultural collaborations with flamenco, blues, jazz, and other international styles of music.
Yandé Codou Sène was a Senegalese singer from the Serer ethnic group.
Youssou N'Dour is a Senegalese singer, songwriter, musician, composer, occasional actor, businessman, and politician.
